---
title: "File compatibility and limitations"
---

## Supported files and preparation

ToFScope reads supported *TOFWERK* *TOFexplorer*[^trademark] HDF5 (`.h5`) acquisitions. A file can contain stored ion
maps or raw events. For raw files without ion maps, [preparation](../using-tofscope/15-raw-preparation.qmd) creates
a new copy with integrated peak data while retaining raw events and metadata. Missing timing or channel metadata requires
explicit acknowledgment of reconstruction assumptions.

## What a saved copy preserves

[Save as](../using-tofscope/14-saving-and-exports.qmd) stores committed analysis settings and full-resolution custom
results in a new HDF5 copy. It also attempts to add eligible named signals as vendor peaks and reports exclusions.
ToFScope restores its own analysis metadata when the saved copy is reopened.

ToFScope cannot guarantee that its output files will be fully supported by *TOFexplorer* or that both
applications will produce identical numerical results. One known gap is that ToFScope allows you to define disjoint
mass windows, but the vendor software does not understand these types of signals.

## Current limitations

Live analyses and jobs are held in memory and do not survive a service restart unless the data is saved to disk.
Shared use requires a trusted authenticated proxy; self-hosted authentication and container deployment remain
under development, and NFS deployment has not been qualified. The [deployment guide](41-deployment.qmd) covers
hosted configurations.

3D rendering is qualitative and uses bounded display previews. The [3D guide](../using-tofscope/13-3d-visualization.qmd)
explains pooling, coverage, interpolation, and rendering limits. Profiles, measurements, and CSV exports use
original-resolution data.

## HDF5 compatibility

The [HDF5 compatibility](32-hdf5-validation.qmd) page describes how saved copies work in ToFScope and the limits of their
use in *TOFexplorer*.

[^trademark]: *TOFWERK* and *TOFexplorer* are names owned by [*TOFWERK AG*](https://www.tofwerk.com/). ToFScope is an independent project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by *TOFWERK AG*.
